Introduction
The book of Culture, Art and Sports has been prepared per the Curriculum and Syllabus for Primary Education of 2023 issued by the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology
This book is the Second Edition, improved from the Sports and Art Book published in 2018 in line with the curriculum of 2016
This book aims to enable the pupil to develop competency in culture, arts and sports through various learning activities in the following areas:
1 Appreciate one’s culture and that of other people;
2 Demonstrate religious tolerance;
3 Demonstrate ethical practice;
4 Creative works of art; and
5 Participate in various sports and games

I identify the activities of Tanzanian communities
Tanzanian communities engage in various activities depending on the nature of their environment
Some of the activities include farming, livestock keeping, fishing and business
These activities contribute to the development of the communities
Livestock keeping
Livestock keeping is an activity that involves taking care of animals and birds
Some of the animals kept are cows, goats, sheep and rabbits
Birds that are kept are chickens, ducks and guineafowls
Livestock keeping helps people to get food and money

Read the passage and answer the questions that follows:
People go to pray so that they become good and kind with acceptable ethics
There are different religions like Islam, Christianity and Hinduism in our community
Praying helps people to be kind, loving, respectful, patient and work together
It also, helps them to avoid bad behaviour such as being greedy, stealing, fighting and being unfaithful

Read the story and answer the questions that follows:
At Amani Primary School there were three pupils named Furaha, Tumaini and Baraka
These pupils were in Standard Two and had different beliefs
They attended different sessions in school, including religious
In the religious session they learn to be loving, patient, cooperative and care for others
Furaha and Tumaini were obedient and eager to attend all sessions
Baraka did not like to participate in religious sessions
During the session, he would rather run away and hide behind the classroom
Because of this behaviour, Baraka was naughty, selfish and did not care about others
One day, the teacher told them the effects of not attending religious sessions
The teacher said, “If you miss the religious sessions you cannot learn good things for the community. Therefore, you will not be a well-behaved child and not accepted by the community”
Furaha and Tumaini decided to talk to Baraka
They advised him to attend religious sessions to learn many good things for the community
Baraka agreed and started attending religious
sessions with other pupils
From that day, Baraka starts to behave nicely
Now, Baraka, Furaha and Tumaini are good and loving children who care for others and do well in their studies

A game of running with a stick
A game of running with a stick involves two teams of two players each
The teams compete to run with a stick in their hands
Players of the same team exchange the stick in the middle of the race
Then, the last receiver runs to the finishing line
How to play:
Prepare the body;
letter A
Walk quickly and run slowly for 2 to 3 minutes;
letter B
Stand and jump for 10 to 15 times; and
letter C
Stretch your body parts for 2 to 3 minutes
Form teams of two players and each team must have one stick;
Draw or use cones to make a circle on the ground with a diameter of 25 steps;
Small cones are placed in a big circle on the ground. A straight line goes through the middle to show the diameter of the circle
The circle is made from a cone
Stand with your opponent on a starting line while holding a stick in your hand;
Make sure your teammate stands at the exchange zone on the opposite of the circle;
Kneel with one leg and hands on the floor behind the starting line;
Two children kneel at the starting line on a track, ready to run with batons in their hands
